question: Film actress Hema Malini is a trained ______ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hema Malini is a veteran Indian film actress and a classically trained Bharatanatyam dancer. (भरतनाट्यम नृत्यांगना — हेमा मालिनी)

 

• She trained under the legendary guru Vempati Chinna Satyam and is regarded as one of India's finest exponents of Bharatanatyam.

 

• She runs her own dance institution, Natya Vihar, and has choreographed and performed several dance-dramas based on Indian mythology, including "Draupadi" and "Durga".

 

• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu and is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, traditionally performed in Hindu temples.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hema Malini was awarded the Padma Shri (2000) and the Padma Bhushan (2012) by the Government of India.

 

• She has also served as a Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha and later Lok Sabha from Mathura).

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 2): A classical dance-drama form of Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes and facial make-up.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): A classical dance form that originated in Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Kathak (Option 4): A classical dance form associated with North India, especially Uttar Pradesh.

question: Who among the following Indian tennis players won the men's doubles title at the Bangkok Open Challenger held at Nonthaburi, Thailand in January 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yuki Bhambri and Saketh Myneni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian pair of Yuki Bhambri and Saketh Myneni won the men's doubles title at the Bangkok Open Challenger (2023 Nonthaburi Challenger II) held at Nonthaburi, Thailand, in January 2023. (बैंकॉक ओपन चैलेंजर — युकी भांबरी व सकेत मयनेनी)

 

• This ATP Challenger Tour event is held annually at the Rajapark Tennis Club, Nonthaburi, Thailand.

 

• Saketh Myneni is a doubles specialist from Andhra Pradesh, while Yuki Bhambri is a Delhi-based player known for both singles and doubles success.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ATP Challenger Tour is the second-highest tier of professional men's tennis, feeding directly into the main ATP Tour.

 

• India has traditionally produced strong doubles specialists, including Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, and Rohan Bopanna.

 

NOTE

 

• Arjun Kadhe and Saketh Myneni (Option 1): Arjun Kadhe is an Indian doubles player but was not Myneni's partner in this particular title.

 

• Rohan Bopanna and Ramkumar Ramanathan (Option 3): Both are accomplished Indian players but did not win this particular title together.

 

• Prithvi Sekhar and Dhananjay Dubey (Option 4): These players were not the winners of this title.

question: Rajaram was the leader of which of the following revolts against the Mughals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram (Rajaram) Jat led the Jat revolt against Mughal rule, continuing the resistance started by his uncle Gokula after the latter's execution. (जाट विद्रोह — राजा राम)

 

• The Jats, peasant cultivators of the region around Mathura and Agra, rose in rebellion during the reign of Aurangzeb, angered by oppressive taxation and religious persecution.

 

• Raja Ram is particularly remembered for looting and desecrating Akbar's tomb at Sikandra in 1688 in retaliation for Mughal atrocities.

 

• The Jat resistance later culminated in the establishment of an independent Bharatpur state under Churaman and Badan Singh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jat uprising began under Gokula of Tilpat in 1669, the first major Jat rebellion against Aurangzeb.

 

• Suraj Mal later made Bharatpur one of the most powerful Jat kingdoms in 18th-century India.

 

NOTE

 

• Satnami (Option 1): The Satnami revolt (1672) was led by peasants and artisans of the Satnami sect near Narnaul, Haryana.

 

• Bundela (Option 2): The Bundela revolt was led by Champat Rai and later his son Chhatrasal against Mughal authority in Bundelkhand.

 

• Munda (Option 4): The Munda Ulgulan (1899-1900) was led by Birsa Munda in Chotanagpur, much later, against British colonial rule, not the Mughals.

question: Which of the following states of India still uses the ancient bamboo drip irrigation method?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The bamboo drip irrigation system is a nearly 200-year-old indigenous technique practised by the War-Khasi and Jaintia tribal communities of Meghalaya. (बांस टपक सिंचाई — मेघालय)

 

• In this system, water from perennial springs and streams is diverted through a network of bamboo pipes to individual plants, especially in betel leaf and areca nut plantations, delivering water drop by drop directly to the roots.

 

• It is one of the most efficient traditional irrigation methods, losing very little water to evaporation or runoff.

 

• This system has been recognised internationally as an excellent example of an indigenous, sustainable water-management technique.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Meghalaya, meaning "abode of clouds", is also home to Mawsynram and Cherrapunji, among the wettest places on Earth.

 

• Traditional irrigation systems in India include Zabo cultivation in Nagaland and Ahar-Pyne systems in Bihar.

 

NOTE

 

• Telangana (Option 1): Not known for the bamboo drip irrigation method; it relies more on tank irrigation and canal systems.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Known for large dam-based and canal irrigation projects, not bamboo drip irrigation.

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 4): Predominantly rice-growing state relying on tank and canal irrigation, not this method.

question: The Family Courts (Amendment) Act 2022 has amended the Family Courts Act, 1984. The Act allows _________________ to establish Family Courts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is State Governments.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Family Courts Act, 1984, as amended in 2022, empowers State Governments, in consultation with the respective High Court, to establish Family Courts. (परिवार न्यायालय अधिनियम — राज्य सरकार)

 

• The Family Courts (Amendment) Act, 2022 was primarily brought in to give retrospective validation to Family Courts already established or notified by certain State Governments (like Himachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Sikkim) without prior High Court consultation, and to enable creation of more such courts.

 

• Family Courts aim at promoting conciliation and securing speedy settlement of disputes relating to marriage and family affairs.

 

• The Act mandates that a State Government may establish a Family Court for every area with a population of one million or more, and may also establish one for any other area it deems necessary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Family Courts primarily deal with matters like divorce, maintenance, custody of children, and matrimonial disputes.

 

• The Act encourages the use of conciliation and mediation over adversarial litigation in family disputes.

 

NOTE

 

• District Courts (Option 1): District Courts are regular civil/criminal courts and are not the establishing authority for Family Courts.

 

• Union Government (Option 3): The subject falls under the domain of State Governments (in consultation with High Courts), not the Union Government.

 

• District Collector (Option 4): An administrative/executive officer, not a judicial authority empowered to establish courts.

question: Who founded the Arya Samaj and pleaded for the right of individuals to interpret Vedas and free themselves from the tyranny of priests?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swami Dayananda Saraswati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875 (headquarters later moved to Lahore). (आर्य समाज — स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती)

 

• He advocated the slogan "Back to the Vedas", urging that every individual has the right to read and interpret the Vedas directly, without dependence on priestly intermediaries.

 

• He condemned idol worship, caste rigidity, child marriage, and priestly domination, and authored the influential text "Satyarth Prakash".

 

• The Arya Samaj also promoted the Shuddhi movement for reconversion and set up DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) schools to spread modern and Vedic education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Swami Dayananda Saraswati was born as Mool Shankar in Tankara, Gujarat.

 

• The Arya Samaj played a significant role in social reform and the growth of nationalist consciousness in northern India.

 

NOTE

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Option 1): Founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828, and campaigned against practices like Sati.

 

• RG Bhandarkar (Option 2): A noted Orientalist and social reformer associated with the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra.

 

• MG Ranade (Option 4): A founder of the Prarthana Samaj and a prominent social reformer and economic thinker of Maharashtra.

question: What is the popular name for mercury(I) chloride which is used as a laboratory reagent and as a depolarizer in dry batteries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calomel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mercury(I) chloride (Hg₂Cl₂) is popularly known as Calomel. (कैलोमेल — मरक्यूरस क्लोराइड)

 

• It is a white, tasteless, odourless solid historically used in medicine (as a purgative and diuretic) and is used as a laboratory reagent and as a depolarizer in dry cell batteries.

 

• It is also used in the construction of the calomel reference electrode, widely employed in electrochemistry to measure electrode potentials.

 

• Chemically, calomel is one of the mercury chlorides, the other being mercury(II) chloride (HgCl₂), known as corrosive sublimate, which is highly toxic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A depolarizer in a battery prevents the accumulation of gas (like hydrogen) around the electrode, which would otherwise reduce battery efficiency.

 

• Common popular names of compounds are frequently asked in GK: e.g. washing soda (sodium carbonate), baking soda (sodium bicarbonate), quicklime (calcium oxide).

 

NOTE

 

• Phosgene (Option 2): Carbonyl chloride (COCl₂), a highly toxic gas used historically as a chemical warfare agent.

 

• Galena (Option 3): The chief ore of lead, chemically lead sulphide (PbS).

 

• Saltpetre (Option 4): The common name for potassium nitrate (KNO₃), used in gunpowder and fertilizers.

question: Which of the following can be considered a part of the parallel economy? (निम्नलिखित में से किसे समानांतर अर्थव्यवस्था का हिस्सा माना जा सकता है?)
option_2: Value of household work done by a housewife (गृहिणी द्वारा किए गए घरेलू कार्य का मूल्य)
option_3: Payments made to domestic helpers or housekeepers (घरेलू सहायकों अथवा हाउसकीपर के लिए किए जाने वाले भुगतान)
option_4: Payments made for private tuition (निजी ट्यूशन के लिए किए जाने वाले भुगतान)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Under-declared income (अल्प घोषित आय).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The parallel economy (also called the black economy or shadow economy) consists of economic activities and income that are not reported or under-reported to tax authorities, and hence escape official national income estimates. (समानांतर अर्थव्यवस्था — अल्प घोषित आय)

 

• Under-declared income is a classic example — income earned but deliberately shown as lower than actual to evade taxes, directly constituting black money, the core of the parallel economy.

 

• The parallel economy typically arises from tax evasion, smuggling, corruption, and other illegal or undisclosed transactions.

 

• Since it goes unrecorded, the parallel economy distorts official GDP estimates and reduces government tax revenue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The problem of black money in India was studied by several committees, including the Wanchoo Committee (1971).

 

• Measures like demonetisation (2016) and the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act aim to curb the parallel economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Value of household work by a housewife (Option 2): This is unpaid, non-market work that is legitimately excluded from GDP calculations, not because it is illegal or undisclosed, but because it lacks a market transaction — it is not part of the parallel economy.

 

• Payments to domestic helpers/housekeepers (Option 3): These are typically small, legitimate service payments, not evasive black-money transactions by nature.

 

• Payments for private tuition (Option 4): While such payments are sometimes undeclared in practice, they are not the defining or textbook example of the parallel economy compared to under-declared income.

question:
In the context of ecology, the given equation shows the relationship between the size of an area and the number of species present in it. Accordingly, by which letter is the regression coefficient denoted?

log S = log C + Z log A
solution_text:
The correct answer is Z.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The equation log S = log C + Z log A represents the species-area relationship in ecology, where S is the number of species, A is the area, C is a constant (the y-intercept), and Z is the regression coefficient (slope of the line). (स्पीशीज-क्षेत्रफल संबंध — प्रतिगमन गुणांक Z)

 

• This relationship was notably studied and used by ecologist Robert MacArthur and biogeographers, and is central to the theory of island biogeography.

 

• The value of Z typically lies in the range of 0.15 to 0.35, regardless of the taxonomic group or region studied, showing a fairly consistent slope for the log-log species-area curve.

 

• On a plot of log S against log A, the slope of the resulting straight line (regardless of the taxonomic group or the region) is remarkably constant — it is this slope, Z, that is the regression coefficient.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Steeper slopes of the species-area curve (higher Z values, around 0.6-1.2) are observed for very large areas, such as entire continents.

 

• The species-area relationship is used to estimate the impact of habitat loss and fragmentation on biodiversity.

 

NOTE

 

• S (Option 1): Represents the number of species, the dependent variable, not the coefficient.

 

• A (Option 2): Represents the area, the independent variable, not the coefficient.

 

• C (Option 4): Represents the constant/intercept of the equation, not the slope/regression coefficient.

question: Which of the following hypothesis was propounded by Harry Hammond Hess in 1962?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sea floor spreading hypothesis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sea Floor Spreading hypothesis was propounded by American geologist Harry Hammond Hess in 1962, in his paper "History of Ocean Basins". (समुद्र तल विस्तार परिकल्पना — हैरी हैमंड हेस)

 

• The theory states that new oceanic crust is continuously formed at mid-oceanic ridges through the upwelling of magma, and the sea floor spreads outward from the ridge, eventually being consumed at subduction zones (ocean trenches).

 

• This hypothesis provided a crucial mechanism to explain continental drift, and was later incorporated into the more comprehensive theory of Plate Tectonics.

 

• Evidence for this theory includes patterns of magnetic striping on the ocean floor, symmetric on either side of mid-oceanic ridges.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Continental Drift theory was proposed earlier, in 1912, by Alfred Wegener.

 

• The Plate Tectonic theory, developed in the late 1960s, unified continental drift and sea floor spreading into a single comprehensive framework.

 

NOTE

 

• Continental Drift hypothesis (Option 1): Proposed by Alfred Wegener in 1912, much earlier than Hess's work.

 

• Gaia hypothesis (Option 3): Proposed by James Lovelock in the 1970s, describing Earth as a self-regulating system.

 

• Geographical cycle hypothesis (Option 4): Also called the "Cycle of Erosion", proposed by William Morris Davis, describing the evolutionary stages of landform development.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about Article 43 B of the Indian Constitution?
option_1: It was added in the 44th Constitutional Amendment.
option_2: It is related to cooperative society.
option_3: It is related with the right of livelihood.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is related to cooperative society.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 43B of the Indian Constitution deals with the "Promotion of Cooperative Societies", directing the State to endeavour to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies. (सहकारी समितियां — अनुच्छेद 43B)

 

• Article 43B was inserted into Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) of the Constitution by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011.

 

• The same 97th Amendment also inserted a new Part IX-B (Articles 243ZH to 243ZT) dealing specifically with cooperative societies, and added the right to form cooperative societies under Article 19(1)(c) as a fundamental right.

 

• In the case of Union of India v. Rajendra N. Shah (2021), the Supreme Court upheld Article 43B but struck down Part IX-B insofar as it applied to state-registered cooperative societies without ratification by states, as it infringed upon state legislative power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India declared 2012 as the "Year of Cooperatives" following the UN's designation of that year as the International Year of Cooperatives.

 

• A separate Ministry of Cooperation was created by the Government of India in July 2021 to provide focused attention to the cooperative sector.

 

NOTE

 

• 44th Constitutional Amendment (Option 1): This amendment (1978) is famous for restoring the balance disturbed by the 42nd Amendment and removing the right to property from fundamental rights, not for Article 43B.

 

• Right to livelihood (Option 3): This is associated with Article 21 (Right to Life), as interpreted judicially, not Article 43B.

 

• Added in 2002 (Option 4): Incorrect year; Article 43B was inserted in 2011, not 2002 (the 86th Amendment of 2002 dealt with the right to education, Article 21A).

question: Which of the following is NOT the first day event in the decathlon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Discus throw.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The decathlon is a two-day, ten-event athletic competition. (डेकाथलॉन — दस स्पर्धाओं की प्रतियोगिता)

 

• The first day events, in order, are: 100 metres, Long jump, Shot put, High jump, and 400 metres.

 

• The second day events are: 110 metres hurdles, Discus throw, Pole vault, Javelin throw, and 1500 metres.

 

• Since Discus throw belongs to the second day's line-up, it is correctly identified as NOT a first-day event.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The women's equivalent multi-event competition is the Heptathlon (seven events over two days).

 

• Scoring in the decathlon is based on standardized points tables for each event, and the athlete with the highest total points wins.

 

NOTE

 

• Shot put (Option 2): This IS a first-day event of the decathlon.

 

• 100 metre dash (Option 3): This IS the very first event of day one in the decathlon.

 

• 400 metre dash (Option 4): This IS the final event of day one in the decathlon.

question: In the women's category, which athlete won the bronze medal at the 2023 Asian 20 km Walking Championships held in Nomi, Japan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Priyanka Goswami.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Priyanka Goswami won the bronze medal in the women's 20 km race walk event, clocking 1:32:27, at the 2023 Asian 20 km Race Walking Championships held in Nomi, Ishikawa, Japan, in March 2023. (एशियाई 20 किमी वॉकिंग चैंपियनशिप — प्रियंका गोस्वामी, कांस्य पदक)

 

• The gold medal was won by Lan Gao of China (1:29:25) and the silver by Ayane Yanai of Japan (1:30:58).

 

• Priyanka Goswami, from Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, is a prominent Indian race walker who had earlier won a silver medal in the women's 10,000m race walk at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham.

 

• In the men's event at the same 2023 championship, Akshdeep Singh won gold, while Vikash Singh and Paramjeet Bisht achieved Paris 2024 Olympic qualification standards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Race walking is an athletic discipline in which contestants must always maintain contact with the ground and keep the leading leg straight until it passes under the body.

 

• Priyanka Goswami later represented India at the 2024 Paris Olympics in race walking events.

 

NOTE

 

• Manju Rani (Option 1): A prominent Indian boxer, not associated with race walking.

 

• Bhawna Jat (Option 3): An Indian race walker and Tokyo Olympian who also competed at this event but finished outside the podium (1:36:20).

 

• Khushbir Kaur (Option 4): An Indian race walker, but was not the bronze medallist at this particular championship.

question: Which of the following is the famous festival of Andhra Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanuma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kanuma is the third day of the Sankranti (Pongal) festivities, dedicated to the worship of cattle, and is widely and traditionally celebrated across present-day Andhra Pradesh. (కనుమ పండుగ — ఆంధ్ర ప్రదేశ్)

 

• On this day, farmers decorate and honour their cattle, bullocks and other livestock in gratitude for their role in agriculture, and elaborate bullock-cart races and cockfights are held in many parts of the state.

 

• There is a popular saying — "Kanuma na kootiki kuda pothaadu" — reflecting how central this day is to Andhra Pradesh's rural culture, even more so than travelling for other occasions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kanuma follows Bhogi and Makara Sankranti, the first two days of the broader Sankranti festival celebrated across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

 

NOTE

 

• Bonalu (Option 3): This is the answer marked in the source PDF's answer key; however, Bonalu — along with Bathukamma — has been officially declared a state festival of Telangana by the Government of Telangana since the state's 2014 bifurcation from Andhra Pradesh, so it is not the festival specifically associated with present-day Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Elephanta (Option 2): Not a festival at all — Elephanta Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage rock-cut cave complex located on Elephanta Island near Mumbai, Maharashtra.

 

• Konark (Option 4): Not a festival at all — Konark is a town in Odisha, famous for the Sun Temple; the "Konark Dance Festival" held there is a classical dance festival, not native to Andhra Pradesh.

question: The second annual session of Indian National Congress was held at which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The second session of the Indian National Congress was held in Calcutta in December 1886, presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji. (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस — द्वितीय अधिवेशन, कलकत्ता)

 

• The first session of the INC was held in Bombay in December 1885, presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee, with 72 delegates attending.

 

• The Indian National Congress was founded largely due to the efforts of Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant.

 

• Holding sessions in different cities each year helped the INC build a pan-India presence and rally nationalist sentiment across regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The third session of the INC was held in Madras in 1887, presided over by Badruddin Tyabji, the first Muslim president of Congress.

 

• Annie Besant was the first woman president of the INC (Calcutta session, 1917).

 

NOTE

 

• Bombay (Option 1): This is where the first INC session was held in 1885, not the second.

 

• Delhi (Option 2): Delhi hosted later INC sessions (e.g., 1918, 1923), not the second session.

 

• Madras (Option 4): Madras hosted the third INC session in 1887, not the second.

question: Yamini Krishnamurthy, a legendary figure of Indian classical dance, was honoured with the ________________ in 2016.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Vibhushan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy, a renowned exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian honour, in 2016. (पद्म विभूषण — यामिनी कृष्णमूर्ति, 2016)

 

• She had earlier also received the Padma Shri (1968) and the Padma Bhushan (2001), making her one of the few artists to receive all three levels of Padma awards.

 

• Trained under gurus like Ellappa Pillai and Pandanallur Chokkalingam Pillai, she was instrumental in popularising both Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi on the national and international stage.

 

• She founded the Yamini School of Dance in New Delhi to train future generations of dancers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are announced annually on the occasion of Republic Day and comprise three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri, in descending order of distinction.

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy passed away in 2024 at the age of 84.

 

NOTE

 

• Saraswati Samman (Option 1): A prestigious literary award given for outstanding prose or poetry, not a civilian honour for dance.

 

• Moortidevi Award (Option 3): A literary award instituted by the Bharatiya Jnanpith, not applicable here.

 

• Bharat Ratna (Option 4): India's highest civilian award; Yamini Krishnamurthy was not conferred this award.

question: Silicon doped with gallium forms ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is p-type semiconductor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Silicon is a group 14 (tetravalent) element, and when doped with gallium, a group 13 (trivalent) element, it forms a p-type semiconductor. (p-टाइप अर्धचालक — सिलिकॉन व गैलियम डोपिंग)

 

• Gallium has only three valence electrons, so when it replaces a silicon atom in the crystal lattice, it creates a "hole" (electron deficiency), which acts as the majority charge carrier.

 

• Since the majority charge carriers are positive holes, the resulting semiconductor is called a p-type (positive-type) semiconductor.

 

• Trivalent dopants like gallium, boron, and indium are known as acceptor impurities, as they "accept" electrons from neighbouring silicon atoms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Doping silicon with a pentavalent (group 15) element like phosphorus or arsenic instead produces an n-type semiconductor, where electrons are the majority carriers.

 

• The p-n junction, formed by joining p-type and n-type semiconductors, is the fundamental building block of diodes and transistors.

 

NOTE

 

• n-type semiconductor (Option 1): Formed by doping with pentavalent elements (like phosphorus), not trivalent gallium.

 

• Superconductor (Option 2): A material with zero electrical resistance, typically achieved at very low temperatures; unrelated to simple doping of silicon.

 

• Insulator (Option 3): A material that does not conduct electricity; doped silicon remains a semiconductor, not an insulator.

question: Bismillah Khan played which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shehnai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan was a legendary Indian classical musician renowned for playing the Shehnai, a wind (reed) instrument. (शहनाई — उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान)

 

• He is widely credited with bringing the Shehnai, traditionally a folk and ceremonial instrument, to the status of a classical concert instrument.

 

• He famously performed from the Red Fort on the eve of India's independence on 15 August 1947, and also played at the Republic Day celebrations of 1950.

 

• In 2001, he was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, becoming only the third classical musician to receive it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bismillah Khan belonged to the Benaras Gharana of Hindustani classical music and lived most of his life in Varanasi.

 

• He was also honoured with the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan before receiving the Bharat Ratna.

 

NOTE

 

• Sitar (Option 1): Associated with musicians like Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Vilayat Khan.

 

• Tabla (Option 3): Associated with tabla maestros like Ustad Zakir Hussain and Pandit Kishan Maharaj.

 

• Harmonium (Option 4): A keyboard reed instrument commonly used to accompany vocal music, not Bismillah Khan's principal instrument.

question:
Match the following items with respect to money.

List I

i. Primary functions

ii. Secondary functions

iii. Evils of money

iv. Contingent functions

List II

a. Distribution of national income

b. Measure of value

c. Store of value

d. Instability of value
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-b, ii-c, iii-d, iv-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the classification of the functions of money (based on the classical Crowther-style categorisation used in economics), money performs primary, secondary, contingent functions, and also gives rise to certain evils. (मुद्रा के कार्य — प्राथमिक, द्वितीयक, आकस्मिक कार्य एवं दोष)

 

• Primary functions (i) are the basic, essential functions of money — acting as a measure of value (b), i.e., a common unit to express and compare the value of goods and services (along with being a medium of exchange).

 

• Secondary functions (ii) are the supportive functions that flow from the primary ones — money acting as a store of value (c), allowing wealth to be saved and used in the future.

 

• Evils of money (iii) refer to the problems that can arise from a money-based economy, chief among them being instability of value (d) — i.e., inflation or deflation eroding money's purchasing power.

 

• Contingent functions (iv) are the indirect or incidental functions, such as helping in the distribution of national income (a) among the factors of production (rent, wages, interest, profit) in the form of money payments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other secondary functions of money include the standard of deferred payments and transfer of value.

 

• Other contingent functions include acting as the basis of credit and helping in maximisation of satisfaction/utility for consumers and producers.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-d, ii-c, iii-a, iv-b): Incorrectly assigns instability of value to primary functions and distribution of income to evils of money.

 

• Option 2 (i-a, ii-d, iii-b, iv-c): Incorrectly assigns distribution of income to primary functions and measure of value to evils of money.

 

• Option 3 (i-c, ii-b, iii-a, iv-d): Incorrectly swaps the primary and secondary function pairings and misassigns the contingent function.

question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty in the Indian Constitution? (निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा भारतीय संविधान में एक मौलिक कर्तव्य नहीं है?)
option_1: To protect public property (सार्वजनिक संपत्ति की रक्षा करना)
option_2: To uphold and protect the sovereignty of the country (देश की संप्रभुता को बनाए रखना और उसकी रक्षा करना)
option_3: To promote harmony and the spirit of brotherhood (सद्भाव और भाईचारे की भावना को बढ़ावा देना)
option_4: To protect monuments (स्मारकों की रक्षा करना)
solution_text:
The correct answer is To protect monuments (स्मारकों की रक्षा करना).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A, under Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• Originally 10 duties were listed; an 11th duty — regarding a parent/guardian's duty to provide education to children aged 6-14 — was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• The listed duties include safeguarding public property (Article 51A(i)), upholding and protecting the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India (51A(c) and 51A(d)), and promoting harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood (51A(e)).

 

• "To protect monuments" is NOT worded as a fundamental duty; the closest related duty is 51A(f) — to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture — but there is no specific duty phrased as protecting monuments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be directly enforced by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

• Article 51A(g) enjoins citizens to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.

 

NOTE

 

• To protect public property (Option 1): This IS a fundamental duty under Article 51A(i).

 

• To uphold and protect the sovereignty of the country (Option 2): This IS a fundamental duty under Article 51A(c)/(d).

 

• To promote harmony and brotherhood (Option 3): This IS a fundamental duty under Article 51A(e).

question: During a boom, the deficit of the government will reduce automatically due to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is increase in tax revenue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During an economic boom, incomes, profits and consumption rise, which automatically leads to an increase in tax revenue (through progressive income tax, corporate tax, and indirect taxes), reducing the government's fiscal deficit without any explicit change in policy. (आर्थिक उछाल — कर राजस्व में वृद्धि)

 

• This phenomenon is a classic example of an automatic stabilizer — a built-in fiscal mechanism that counteracts economic fluctuations without discretionary government intervention.

 

• Progressive taxation means that as incomes rise during a boom, a larger proportion of income is collected as tax, further boosting revenue and moderating the deficit.

 

• Conversely, during a recession, tax revenues automatically fall and government spending on unemployment benefits/welfare rises, automatically widening the deficit — again without new policy action.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Automatic stabilizers include progressive income taxes and unemployment insurance/welfare payments.

 

• They are distinguished from discretionary fiscal policy, where the government deliberately changes tax rates or spending levels to influence the economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Increase in GDP (Option 2): GDP growth is associated with a boom but is not itself the direct mechanism reducing the fiscal deficit — it is the resulting rise in tax revenue that does so.

 

• Decrease in tax revenue (Option 3): This is the opposite of what happens during a boom; tax revenue rises, not falls.

 

• Decrease in GDP (Option 4): A decrease in GDP is characteristic of a recession, not a boom.

question: What percentage of the Indian population was estimated to be living below the poverty line in 2011-12?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21.9%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the estimates based on the Tendulkar Committee methodology, 21.9% of India's population was estimated to be living below the poverty line in 2011-12. (गरीबी रेखा — 21.9%, 2011-12)

 

• This was a decline from 37.2% in 2004-05, reflecting a significant reduction in poverty over that period.

 

• The Tendulkar Committee, headed by economist Suresh Tendulkar, revised the poverty line methodology to base it on Mixed Reference Period (MRP) consumption and included expenditure on health and education, besides food.

 

• Rural poverty in 2011-12 was estimated at around 25.7%, while urban poverty was around 13.7%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rangarajan Committee later proposed an alternative poverty estimate for 2011-12 of about 29.5%, using a different methodology, though the Tendulkar estimates (21.9%) remain the more commonly cited official figure.

 

• Poverty estimation in India has historically used the calorie-based norm, first defined by the Y.K. Alagh Committee.

 

NOTE

 

• 25.6% (Option 1): Not the accepted figure for 2011-12 under the Tendulkar methodology.

 

• 10.9% (Option 2): Too low and does not match any official estimate for this period.

 

• 15.6% (Option 3): Does not match the official Tendulkar Committee estimate for 2011-12.

question: The Himalayan Mountains act as an effective climatic divide by protecting the subcontinent from:
solution_text:
The correct answer is cold northern winds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Himalayas act as an effective climatic divide, shielding the Indian subcontinent from the bitterly cold winds blowing from Central Asia during winter. (हिमालय — शीत उत्तरी पवनों से रक्षा)

 

• Without this barrier, cold Siberian/Central Asian air masses would sweep unhindered into the Indian plains, making Indian winters far more severe.

 

• Because of this protective effect, North India experiences a relatively milder winter compared to regions at similar latitudes elsewhere in Asia (like Central Asia or Mongolia).

 

• The Himalayas also help trap the monsoon winds, forcing them to shed their moisture over the Indian subcontinent rather than passing further north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Himalayas form a nearly continuous arc of about 2,400 km, stretching from Jammu & Kashmir in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east.

 

• They are geologically young fold mountains, formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates.

 

NOTE

 

• Warm southern winds (Option 2): These are not obstructed by the Himalayas, which lie to the north of India; southern winds are not the relevant phenomenon here.

 

• Cyclonic winds (Option 3): Tropical cyclones affecting India typically originate over the Bay of Bengal/Arabian Sea and are unrelated to the Himalayan barrier.

 

• Western disturbances (Option 4): These are extratropical storms originating over the Mediterranean region that bring winter rain/snow to North India; the Himalayas do not "protect" against them — in fact, they interact with them to cause snowfall in the hills.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the common goals of five year plans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Globalisation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The common, long-standing goals of India's Five Year Plans have traditionally been identified as Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance, and Equity. (पंचवर्षीय योजनाएं — वृद्धि, आधुनिकीकरण, आत्मनिर्भरता, समानता)

 

• Growth refers to increasing the country's capacity to produce goods and services (raising national/per-capita income).

 

• Modernisation refers to adopting new technology and evolving institutional/social structures (e.g., according women greater rights).

 

• Self-reliance meant reducing dependence on foreign goods, especially food grains and capital equipment, a goal emphasised heavily from the Third Five Year Plan onward.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Equity was included as a goal to ensure that the benefits of economic growth reach all sections of society, especially the poorer sections.

 

• Though the Indian economy embraced greater globalisation after the 1991 economic reforms, it is not traditionally listed among the core, universally common goals across all Five Year Plans.

 

NOTE

 

• Self-reliance (Option 1): This IS one of the traditional common goals of the Five Year Plans.

 

• Modernisation (Option 2): This IS one of the traditional common goals of the Five Year Plans.

 

• Growth (Option 4): This IS one of the traditional common goals of the Five Year Plans.

question: The novel Self-Help Group Bank Linkage Program (SHG-BLP) project which grew into a dominant micro finance model, was piloted by ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Self-Help Group Bank Linkage Programme (SHG-BLP) was piloted by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) in 1992. (स्वयं सहायता समूह-बैंक संबद्धता कार्यक्रम — नाबार्ड)

 

• It links informal women's/rural Self-Help Groups (SHGs) with the formal banking system, enabling them to access credit without traditional collateral, based on group guarantee.

 

• SHG-BLP grew to become the world's largest microfinance programme in terms of outreach, playing a major role in promoting financial inclusion and empowering rural women in India.

 

• NABARD is the apex development bank in India, established in 1982, responsible for facilitating credit flow for agriculture and rural development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD also promotes rural infrastructure through funds like the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF).

 

• The SHG-BLP model has been widely studied internationally as a successful example of a microfinance and financial inclusion initiative.

 

NOTE

 

• MFI (Option 2): Refers to Micro Finance Institutions in general (a category of lenders), not the specific body that piloted the SHG-BLP programme.

 

• IRDA (Option 3): The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority, which regulates the insurance sector, unrelated to SHG-BLP.

 

• SEBI (Option 4): The Securities and Exchange Board of India, the regulator for the securities market, unrelated to SHG-BLP.
